content: To the entire world, including the gods,You proclaim the lion’s roarOf the eighty-four thousand gateways of Dharma,Peerless one, I pray at the feet of the learned and accomplished Lord of Dharma.In the glorious Shambhala, the supreme land of accomplishment,You became the chief of the lineage, the Kalki,Renowned as Gelek Pal, the crown jewelOf all the scholars on this earth, I pray to you.To those who falsely claim to be learned in this quarter,Your roar of scripture and reasoning is unbearable;You are renowned in the three worlds as the crown jewel of orators,Who strikes great fear into them, I pray to you.Having realized the meaning of phenomena as being like an illusion,You teach the fortunate ones directly, saying,"I have awakened to buddhahood in a manner like an illusion,"Powerful Vajradhara, I pray to you.Though you always dwell in the state of the great bliss Dharmakaya,You uphold the ways of the learned and accomplished,Such as the foremost son of Nāgārjuna, Bhavaviveka,And Abhayākara, supreme Guru, I pray to you.The embodiment of all Victors, the venerable Tsongkhapa’sForemost son, the incomparable Dge-legs-dpal,By the merit arising from this slight praise,May all beings be possessed of the supreme vehicle’s protector.In this quarter, through the enlightened activity of the Guru, father and sons,Like the Lord of Day blazing with a thousand rays,May all the masses of darkness of wrong views be uprooted,And the hundred-petaled lotus of benefit and happiness forever bloom.This was spoken at the great monastic seat of Rtses-thang by the monk Dge-'dun-rgya-mtsho-dpal-bzang-po, at the request of several earnest seekers.
